_meta.purpose: IMDA Model AI Governance Framework (May 2026) in CatalogFile shape, so applyCatalogFile creates the framework, its requirements, the templates, their requirement links and the pack together.
_meta.why: Built inline in prisma/seed.ts, which is not run on production deploys. Production has never held this framework — not the framework row, not the templates, not the pack. Extracted from a database seeded by the inline block, so the shape is carried over exactly rather than re-derived from the grouping logic.
_meta.grounding: Requirement codes, titles and sections, and the template titles, categories, frequencies and requirement links, are exactly those the inline block produced. Task content is NOT authored here — every template carries the generic five, as it did inline.

framework.name: IMDA Model AI Governance Framework (May 2026)
framework.description: Four AI-governance dimensions — bound risks upfront, meaningful human accountability, technical controls and processes, end-user responsibility — extended for agentic deployments.

metadata.copyright: Model AI Governance Framework © Infocomm Media Development Authority / Personal Data Protection Commission, Singapore. Source: https://www.imda.gov.sg/. Inflect stores dimension titles and its own governance summaries with attribution, not the verbatim publication prose; requirement identifiers are Inflect-assigned and are not IMDA clause numbers. Not legal advice.

requirements.title: Risk taxonomy and tolerances defined before deployment
Internal governance structure with named accountable owners
Agent scope and authority limits are declared and enforced
Third-party agent due diligence before adoption
Human involvement model chosen per decision class
Every deployed agent has an accountable human owner
Automation bias mitigated in human review
Data governance and provenance for inputs and memory
Pre-release and ongoing testing, evaluation and red-teaming
Traceability of decisions, tool calls and actions
Least-privilege identity and credential handling for agents
Incident detection, response and post-incident review
Controls on inter-agent communication and delegation
Disclosure that an AI agent is in use
Capabilities, limits and failure modes explained
User control, consent and redress channels
Guidance for safe operation and against over-reliance

pack.name: IMDA MGF Baseline Pack
pack.description: One control per MGF governance dimension.
